newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals down sharply, gold eyes support.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals down sharply, gold eyes support.

text.p: New York precious metals opened broadly lower as expected Monday morning as uncertainty over Germany's plan to revalue its gold reserves continued to weigh on sentiment, dealers said.
COMEX June Gold broke through a nearby chart barrier at $342.00 an ounce, falling to a low of $340.70 amid steady fund selling. At 0920 EDT, June was down $4.00 at $340.90.

Gold prices have sagged since Germany announced late last week it would revalue the Bundesbank's gold reserves closer to market value. The news rattled the bullion market, despite German denials that any gold would be sold.
"It has put a cloud on the market," said a trader of prospects for central bank sales.
Scattered shortcovering by day traders braked the sell-off, but June futures looked poised to test recent lows of $338 to $340 before the day's end, dealers said.
After a listless opening, silver also took a beating, with benchmark July down 4.30 cents at $4.65. The contract briefly touched a contract low of $462.50 before rebounding.
Platinum and palladium fell as well, hit by steady commercial selling. July platinum was down $5.20 at $386.00, up from a low of 385.50. Stops were well placed below $384.00, traders said.
"Relatively speaking, platinum and palladium are holding up a lot better than gold and silver, but you can't expect a good rally with gold and silver so weak," said a PGM trader.

Earlier Monday, refiner Johnson Matthey predicted the use of platinum in auto catalysts could decline this year in the U.S., though any downturn in demand would likely be compensated by growth elsewhere in the Americas.
Otherwise, precious metals market awaited the results of tomorrow's Federal Open Market Committee meeting to see if the Fed would hike interest rates.
